claim: The grafana-cli accessor returns the new proxy token without any feature-flag check, so the CLI uses a different credential than the server whenever the flag is off and proxy_token is set.
raw: `ContextCommandLine.GrafanaComProxyAPIToken()` returns `cfg.GrafanaComProxyAPIToken` whenever it is non-empty, with no flag check. `grafana-cli` never initializes OpenFeature (verified: zero `openfeature` references under `pkg/cmd/grafana-cli/`), so it *cannot* evaluate the flag as structured. `install_command.go:102` routes plugin installs through it.

claim: The documentation tells operators to enable `dedicatedGrafanaComProxyAPIToken`, but the registered toggle is `grafana.dedicatedGrafanaComProxyAPIToken`, so following the docs silently leaves the feature off.
raw: F2 - Documentation names a toggle that does not exist - Docs say "Requires the `dedicatedGrafanaComProxyAPIToken` feature toggle to be enabled." The registered name is `grafana.dedicatedGrafanaComProxyAPIToken` (`pkg/services/featuremgmt/registry.go:2253`), and that exact literal is what `setting.go:763` evaluates. The undotted form is a *deleted prior name* of this same flag.

claim: Resolution is enforced only by a doc comment, so a skipped Resolve() call now yields an empty token and an entirely unauthenticated Grafana.com proxy request — a regression that was impossible before.
raw: "Must be called after OpenFeature is initialized" is enforced only by a doc comment. `proxy_token` defaults to `""` (`setting.go:1677`), and `ReverseProxyGnetReq` omits the `Authorization` header entirely when the token is empty (`pkg/api/grafana_com_proxy.go:44-46`). ... `testinfra.go:124` initializes OpenFeature and starts a full server serving `/api/gnet/*` without resolving.

claim: Resolve() overwrites the parsed proxy_token with the SSO token using one field as both input and output, making it non-idempotent and destroying the operator-configured value; the flag also lacks RequiresRestart despite being snapshotted at startup.
raw: `cfg.GrafanaComProxyAPIToken = cfg.GrafanaComSSOAPIToken` uses one field as both input and output, destroying the parsed `proxy_token` whenever the flag is off. A second call (flag now on) sees a non-empty field and returns early, permanently pinning the SSO token. Nothing can afterwards answer "was a dedicated token configured?"

claim: The resolver logs none of its three outcomes, so an operator cannot tell whether the dedicated token, the SSO fallback, or no token at all is in use when Grafana.com requests start failing.
raw: The resolver has three outcomes (dedicated / flag-on-but-unset fallback / flag-off fallback discarding a configured token) and logs none of them. `grafana_com_proxy.go:44` silently omits auth on an empty token. When the plugin catalog starts returning 401/403 in production there is no log line distinguishing "using dedicated token", "fell back to SSO", "no token at all".

claim: The feature-flag name is a hardcoded string literal instead of the generated constant, so a future rename compiles cleanly and silently disables the feature.
raw: Duplicates `featuremgmt.FlagGrafanaDedicatedGrafanaComProxyAPIToken` (`toggles_gen.go:727`). The import cycle is real and verified (`featuremgmt/openfeature.go:7` imports `setting`), so this is a forced workaround, not negligence. But `toggles_gen.json` records this flag renamed **four times in eight days**; the fifth rename will compile cleanly and silently disable the feature.

claim: None of the three switched consumers (grafana-cli accessor, the gnet reverse proxy, the plugin config) has any test asserting the new token, so reverting any of the one-line switches would not fail a test.
raw: `pkg/cmd/grafana-cli/utils` has **no test files at all** (verified via `go test ./pkg/cmd/grafana-cli/...`), so the new accessor and its config-error branch are entirely untested. `pkg/api/grafana_com_proxy.go` has zero tests for `ReverseProxyGnetReq`/`ProxyGnetRequest`. `pluginconfig/config_test.go` has no token assertion. `install_command_test.go:103` still asserts `c.GcomToken()`.

claim: The docs scope the token to plugin catalog browsing and grafana-cli installs, but it actually backs the whole /api/gnet/* proxy, the community dashboard library, and admin-API plugin installs, with no scoping or rotation guidance.
raw: Docs scope it to "plugin catalog browsing and plugin installs via `grafana-cli`". Verified, the token actually backs: the entire `/api/gnet/*` reverse proxy (`pkg/api/api.go:587`, `r.Any` behind `reqSignedIn` only); the **community dashboard library**; **admin-API plugin installs** (`pkg/api/api.go:449`). No required token type, scopes, or rotation guidance is stated.

claim: GcomToken() is no longer called by production code but remains on the interface, its impl, and the mock, leaving two near-identical accessors with inconsistent naming.
raw: After `install_command.go:102` switched over, the only remaining references are the interface, its impl, the mock (`command_line_mock.go:149`), and two tests. Every implementer now carries two near-identical accessors that differ only in fallback, with inconsistent naming (`Gcom` vs `GrafanaCom`) in the same interface. The widening was only necessary because the old method was left behind.

claim: The new docs use a relref link that is the only one in the whole setup-grafana tree (against the AGENTS.md convention) and its anchor is likely wrong, which would break the Hugo build.
raw: `{{< relref "#feature_toggles" >}}` is the **only** `relref` in the entire `docs/sources/setup-grafana/` tree, and `docs/AGENTS.md:110` mandates inline Markdown links. ... so the real anchor for `### \`[feature_toggles]\`` is very likely `#feature-toggles`. *[Unverified: I could not render the Hugo site to confirm the generated anchor id.]*

claim: defaults.ini gained proxy_token but the [grafana_com] block in sample.ini was not given a matching commented entry, so the setting is undiscoverable outside the docs site.
raw: F11 - `conf/sample.ini` not updated - `defaults.ini:1899` gains `proxy_token`, but the `[grafana_com]` block in `sample.ini` - which already carries `;url`, `;api_url`, and a commented `;sso_api_token` - was not given a matching entry. `sample.ini` is the file operators copy to `custom.ini`, so the setting is undiscoverable outside the docs site.

claim: The Cfg field and method comments do not disclose the field's two-phase meaning (raw vs effective) nor that the fallback is a destructive overwrite that never happens on the grafana-cli path.
raw: F12 - `Cfg` field comment omits the two-phase lifecycle - The field comment gives no indication that the value means "raw `proxy_token`" before `Resolve()` and "effective token" after, nor that resolution never happens on the `grafana-cli` path. The method comment says "falls back to sso_api_token" without disclosing that this is a *destructive overwrite* of an operator-configured value.

claim: The cfg: override path skips any key containing a dot, so enabling this dotted toggle via cfg:feature_toggles.* is a silent no-op (pre-existing, not introduced by the PR).
raw: `if keyName == "" || strings.Contains(keyName, ".") { continue }` means `cfg:feature_toggles.grafana.dedicatedGrafanaComProxyAPIToken=true` is a silent no-op. Pre-existing infrastructure affecting all dotted flags, not introduced here - but it removes one standard enablement mechanism for this toggle, and the new docs point at `[feature_toggles]` generically.

claim: Dismissed: four stale tombstoned toggle entries in toggles_gen.json are normal generator behavior, not hand-edited clutter.
raw: **Four "stale" toggle entries in `toggles_gen.json`** - 98 tombstoned entries already exist at base vs. 102 at HEAD; retaining deleted-flag history is normal generator behavior, not hand-edited clutter.

claim: Dismissed: setting skipStaticRootValidation = true without restoring it matches the existing package convention and is inherited, not introduced.
raw: **`skipStaticRootValidation = true` without restore** (`setting_test.go:388`) - matches the existing package convention (`setting_test.go:30`, `setting_session_test.go:13`). Inherited, not introduced.

claim: Dismissed: discarding the evaluation error from openfeature.Boolean() is consistent with the codebase-wide idiom.
raw: **`openfeature.Boolean()` discarding the evaluation error** - consistent with the codebase-wide idiom (`pkg/expr/graph.go:242`, `pkg/api/datasources_k8s.go:139`, and ~4 others).

claim: Dismissed: a data race on Resolve() is speculative because it is called once before serving begins.
raw: **Data race on `Resolve()`** - called once before serving begins; speculative.

claim: Dismissed: the missing comment on the new defaults.ini entry matches its uncommented siblings in the same stanza.
raw: **Missing comment on `defaults.ini:1899`** - its siblings in the same stanza are uncommented too.
